headline: Batiste's walk-off grand slam caps five-run ninth
recap: The Phillies trailed the Mets 5-4 entering the bottom of the ninth when John Kruk led off with a walk against reliever Pete Schourek. Two outs later, Pete Incaviglia walked off Anthony Young and Jim Eisenreich reached on a throwing error by shortstop Kevin Baez that let Kruk score the tying run. An intentional walk to Kevin Stocker loaded the bases, and Kim Batiste hit a walk-off grand slam off Young, sending Philadelphia to a 9-5 win.

Terry Mulholland started for the Phillies and allowed five runs, three earned, on eight hits over eight innings, with Bobby Bonilla touching him for solo home runs in the second and fourth. Frank Tanana started for New York and gave up three runs on four hits in six innings, all three scoring on a Wes Chamberlain home run in the second that also drove in Dave Hollins and Darren Daulton.

New York moved ahead 5-3 in the eighth when Dave Gallagher's single, aided by a throwing error from first baseman John Kruk, scored pinch-runner Ced Landrum and Bonilla and let Gallagher himself come around too; Lenny Dykstra's groundout brought Kevin Stocker home in the bottom half to make it 5-4. Bobby Thigpen pitched a scoreless ninth in relief of Mulholland to earn the win, while Young was charged with the loss.
